\begin{document}
\maketitle
\begin{enumerate}[leftmargin=*]
  \item \duallayerbox{In the BIO tagging scheme for NER, what does the ``B-'' prefix indicate?}{In BIO tagging for NER, which tag marks tokens strictly inside an entity span?}
    \textbf{A.} Beginning of an entity
    \textbf{B.} Inside an entity
    \textbf{C.} Outside any entity
    \textbf{D.} Between two tokens

  \item \duallayerbox{Which statement best describes a (plain) Markov chain in sequence tagging?}{In sequence tagging, which option describes a model that uses only the observed words and ignores labels?}
    \textbf{A.} It uses only words (observations) and ignores labels
    \textbf{B.} It is identical to an HMM
    \textbf{C.} It models transitions between labels but does not consider the words
    \textbf{D.} It models emissions P(word | label)

  \item \duallayerbox{In a Hidden Markov Model (HMM) for NER, an emission probability is:}{In an HMM for NER, which probability defines transitions between successive labels?}
    \textbf{A.} P(label | previous label)
    \textbf{B.} P(label | word)
    \textbf{C.} P(word | previous word)
    \textbf{D.} P(word | label)

  \item \duallayerbox{Which of the following best describes Semantic Role Labeling (SRL)?:}{Which option describes a process that assigns grammatical roles like subject and object based on syntax?}
    \textbf{A.} A task that identifies predicates in a sentence and labels roles of elements such as agent, theme, or location
    \textbf{B.} A process that assigns grammatical roles like subject and object based on syntactic structure
    \textbf{C.} A method that classifies named entities and links them to a knowledge base
    \textbf{D.} A technique that labels words with their parts of speech and morphological features

  \item \duallayerbox{Which of the following best describes Byte Pair Encoding (BPE)?}{Which option describes compressing text by replacing repeated character runs with a count and symbol?}
    \textbf{A.} A technique that compresses text by replacing consecutive repeated characters with a count and a symbol
    \textbf{B.} A tokenization method that iteratively merges the most frequent pair of symbols in a corpus
    \textbf{C.} A tokenization method that splits text based on whitespace and punctuation
    \textbf{D.} A character-level encoding scheme that assigns fixed-length binary codes to characters

  \item \duallayerbox{Which of the following best describes the main goal of tokenization in NLP?}{Which option describes assigning each token a grammatical category such as noun or verb?}
    \textbf{A.} To label each token with a grammatical category
    \textbf{B.} To convert text into a sequence of symbols suitable for modeling
    \textbf{C.} To reduce vocabulary size to zero
    \textbf{D.} To assign probabilities to sentences

  \item \duallayerbox{Why is splitting text by spaces (text.split(" ")) considered an insufficient tokenizer?}{What is one criticism of a tokenizer that oversegments text into an unnecessarily large number of tokens?}
    \textbf{A.} It produces too many tokens
    \textbf{B.} It does not work well for languages without explicit word boundaries
    \textbf{C.} It cannot tokenize English at all
    \textbf{D.} It ignores punctuation entirely

  \item \duallayerbox{Which of the following is NOT listed as a common sequence tagging task?}{Which of the following is a classic sequence tagging task that labels each word with its part of speech?}
    \textbf{A.} Part-of-speech tagging
    \textbf{B.} Named Entity Recognition
    \textbf{C.} Dependency parsing
    \textbf{D.} Sentiment analysis

  \item \duallayerbox{What is a common limitation of BIO tagging for Named Entity Recognition?}{In BIO tagging for NER, which issue involves needing too many distinct labels for practical use?}
    \textbf{A.} It cannot represent overlapping or nested entities
    \textbf{B.} It requires too many labels
    \textbf{C.} It does not support multiple entity types
    \textbf{D.} It ignores entity boundaries

  \item \duallayerbox{When choosing between character-level tokenization and sentence-level tokenization, which trade-off must be considered?}{In evaluating an NLP model, which trade-off compares how fast it runs to how accurate it is?}
    \textbf{A.} Speed vs accuracy
    \textbf{B.} Tokenized sequence length vs vocabulary size
    \textbf{C.} Precision vs recall
    \textbf{D.} Memory vs computation

\end{enumerate}
\end{document}
